title: Without the Moon, Lions Win
topic: Without the Moon every night is moonless: about 100x darker than under a full Moon; Serengeti lions eat best on dark nights (Packer et al. 2011), so every night would be a hunting night

beats.narration: If the Moon vanished tonight, lions would be the happiest animals on Earth.
On a clear night, a full Moon lights the ground about a hundred times more than the stars alone. Without it, every night becomes the darkest kind of night. Forever.
phrases: On a clear night, a full

beats.narration: Take lions. In the Serengeti, lions eat best on dark nights, when there's no moonlight to give them away. Around the full Moon, their bellies are emptier, and they have to hunt more by day.
phrases: and they have to hunt more

beats.narration: So without the Moon, every single night is a hunter's night. Great news for lions. Not such great news for everything they eat.
Note to self: never be a zebra.
